# contain

```go
import "github.com/jbcom/radioactive-ralph/internal/contain"
```

Package contain puts a KERNEL\-ENFORCED write boundary around a provider process.

This is deliberately not what internal/orch's secureProjectPath does. That validates path strings Ralph itself handles — which files Ralph will read, and which declared outputs Ralph will admit — and \#228 added detection at completion. None of it constrains the provider: it is a separate process opening files by pathname, minutes later, and no string Ralph returns ever travels into its syscalls. Validation can say "this task declared an escaping path"; only the kernel can say "this process may not write there".

The two layers are complementary. Validation catches the honest mistake early, with a good error. Containment is what makes the guarantee true when the provider does something the declaration did not describe.

## Variables

<a name="ErrContainmentUnavailable"></a>ErrContainmentUnavailable reports a platform with no write\-containment primitive.

Returned rather than silently passing the command through: a caller that believes it is contained when it is not is making exactly the false guarantee this package exists to replace.

```go
var ErrContainmentUnavailable = errors.New("contain: no write containment primitive on this platform")
```

<a name="ErrRootNotAbsolute"></a>ErrRootNotAbsolute reports a containment root that is not an absolute path.

A relative root resolves against whatever working directory the provider inherits, so the boundary would guard a different directory than the caller meant — and would report success while doing it.

```go
var ErrRootNotAbsolute = errors.New("contain: containment root must be an absolute path")
```

<a name="Available"></a>
## func [Available](<https://github.com/jbcom/radioactive-ralph/blob/main/internal/contain/contain.go#L76>)

```go
func Available() bool
```

Available reports whether this platform can enforce a write boundary.

Callers check it to decide policy — refuse to dispatch, or proceed with the weaker validation\-only guarantee — rather than discovering at Wrap time.

<a name="Policy"></a>
## type [Policy](<https://github.com/jbcom/radioactive-ralph/blob/main/internal/contain/contain.go#L40-L46>)

Policy is a resolved write boundary: the provider may write beneath Root and nowhere else.

```go
type Policy struct {
    // Root is the ABSOLUTE, SYMLINK-RESOLVED directory the provider may write
    // under. Resolved because a policy written against a symlink names the link
    // rather than its target, so a provider writing through the resolved path
    // would land outside a boundary that appears to contain it.
    Root string
}
```

<a name="Policy.Wrap"></a>
### func \(Policy\) [Wrap](<https://github.com/jbcom/radioactive-ralph/blob/main/internal/contain/contain.go#L65>)

```go
func (p Policy) Wrap(name string, args []string) (string, []string, error)
```

Wrap rewrites a command so it runs under the policy, returning the name and args to execute.

It returns ErrContainmentUnavailable where no primitive exists. Callers decide whether that is fatal; this package will not pretend.
